facts.d17_cliffside_contact_caller_residual: The caller that decides a Cliffside hit occurred (STILL_OPEN residual) is very likely FUNC_8004ABF4 (Canon: actor_player_contact_resolver / proximity_updater_8004abf4, span 0x8004ABF4-0x8004B6D8), which is confirmed to already be one of FUNC_8004A700's 6 statically-enumerated callers (via its 0x8004B4A0 call site, per FUNC_8004A700's own Canon page) and which -- per its OWN Canon doc -- iterates the live actor table at 0x80090748 doing per-actor proximity/contact dispatch against Flik. Live-confirmed this pass: id=30 occupies SLOT 0 of that table during the Cliffside encounter (0x80090748 itself, not an offset into it), which is exactly the single actor FUNC_8004ABF4's own partially-decoded entry math reads via G_TYPE6_ACTOR_PTR. However, that entry-math's specific radius/threshold check (dx^2+dy^2+dz^2 < r^2 using the +0x6a radius field and a -7360 Y-bias) evaluates to NOT-inside at every sampled frame including the closest approach (f327) -- so while the caller is now well-evidenced by actor-slot identity and call-graph membership, the EXACT branch/threshold inside this function's undecoded body that actually fires the contact is still not pinned. Not a full closure of that residual, but a substantial narrowing (from 'completely unknown' to 'this specific already-Canon function, exact branch TBD').
facts.d17_bit10_search_scope: Exhaustively checked this pass, still open. debugger.xrefsTo on 0x800A6590 (power-flags word) was run against BOTH the Birdnest (D17.movie.sav) and Cliffside (D17_Cliffside_Bird_Death.movie.sav) resident RAM images -- both return the SAME 8 static store sites (0x8001d5f8, 0x8004a7b0, 0x8004a8e0, 0x80051eb0, 0x80054e90, 0x8005b340, 0x8005d088, 0x800b3d3c), and every one was individually disassembled: none ORs in bit 0x10 (immediates found: 0x0001, 0x0002 x2, 0x0080, 0x0020 (andi), 0x0004 x2). A parallel grep of the entire hand-disassembled resident ASM corpus (asm/nonmatchings/resident/*.s, the 23 files that reference 0x6590) for an ori/andi immediate of 0x10 near a 0x6590 store also found nothing. The bit-0x10 writer is therefore almost certainly OVERLAY code specific to Cliffside (F04) that is not in the current disassembled corpus at all, or uses an addressing pattern (computed/indirect base) that a literal lui+offset static scan does not catch -- not a resident, already-documented writer being mis-attributed.

THE ROW'S OWN NAMED RESIDUAL IS MIS-SHAPED, and a compiled-C decode of all 21 shipped images shows it. D17's negative on power bit 0x10 came from 8 addresses in one resident RAM image and concluded the writer is 'almost certainly OVERLAY code specific to Cliffside'. The full static census finds 19 stores to that word (15 resident + 4 overlay), a superset of D17's list, setting masks ['0x1', '0x2', '0x4', '0x8', '0x20', '0x80'] and AND-masking ['0x20', '0xFEFF', '0xFF7E', '0xFFF7', '0xFFFB']. NONE writes bit 0x10, and the Cliffside overlay's single power-flags store is an OR of 0x4. The negative survives a much wider search -- which is good news -- but the hypothesis attached to it does not, so the residual should be re-stated as 'pointer-relative or unindexed writer', not 'uncharted Cliffside overlay'.

A CANDIDATE FOR THE STAGE'S PUNISHMENT PATH IS SITTING IN AN ARTIFACT THE ROW NEVER READ. The Cliffside overlay's own 10 indexed code functions (['clear_overlay_state', 'level06_select_grid_offset', 'level_overlay_init', 'level_spawn_handler', 'level_state_writer', 'level_state_writer_c98', 'level_transition_handler', 'transition_handler_arg_entry']) include ONE that owns every candidate PC below -- derived by containment, not asserted: [('LEVEL06_LEVEL', '0x800B3BC4', 'level_transition_handler')] owns all of ['LEVEL06_LEVEL:0x800B3CD4', 'LEVEL06_LEVEL:0x800B3D3C', 'LEVEL06_LEVEL:0x800B3EA4'] (single owner: True). That one function reads the player's grounded flag, read-modify-writes the power word, and stores the scene-transition request. Across the campaign, 10 level overlays store request constant 1 and exactly 1 stores constant 2 -- ['LEVEL06_LEVEL'] ([{'pc': '0x800B3EA4', 'form': 'const', 'value': 2}]); ['LEVEL02_LEVEL'] had an unrecovered value and are not counted either way. What is request 2? The resident writers of that constant are ['0x8004A8B4', '0x8004A9F4'], and they resolve to ['asm/hand_written/8004a700_resident_level_transition_initiator.s'] -- i.e. the player damage handler, the same function whose stagger store at 0x8004a814 is D17's observed Cliffside death path. That is a STATIC CANDIDATE ONLY -- no trace has ever put a PC in this overlay, F04's watches were all resident addresses, and nothing here proves this function runs in the bird encounter. But it is exactly the shape D17 described behaviourally (land -> freeze -> fade -> lives-1) and it is one exec watch away from being decided.
